_comment: The five pillars: the one definition both apps and the backend read.
JSON rather than TypeScript because the consumers include two tailwind.config
files (CommonJS, cannot require a .ts module) and a Flask backend. A
TypeScript file cannot be canonical for a Python process, so scripts/
generate-constants.mjs emits BOTH languages from this file, and CI fails if
the emitted files drift from it. Do not hand-edit anything under generated/.
Colours follow docs/COLOR_REFERENCE.md, which is the brand reference.
History worth keeping: the web app and backend/config/pillars.py rendered civics and
wellness in each other's colours until 2026-09-04, so the same pillar was
orange on the web and red on mobile. Extracting this file is what surfaced it.
It is fixed everywhere now, and mobile/src/__tests__/pillarPalette.test.ts
checks every file that still spells a pillar hex against this one -- including
the web app's -light/-dark shades and gradients, which are web-only and so cannot live
here, and are the part most likely to be flipped back to match a stale
screenshot.
`legacy` is emitted to PYTHON ONLY. It is the pre-2025 vocabulary -- the
underscore keys, the short keys and the '&' display names -- which the
backend still has to accept because rows written before the rename are still
in the database and the AI prompts were written against it. It was declared
four separate times (utils/pillar_utils.py, prompts/components.py,
routes/personalization_validators.py, services/roster_import_service.py) and
the copies did not agree. Neither client has ever needed it, so the
TypeScript output leaves it out: what a surface does not need, it should not
be able to read.
